subject: Materials Science
title: Magnetic Properties of Materials
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Magnetic Properties of Materials.

hook.text: A magnet sticks to your fridge but not to aluminum foil — only certain materials are ferromagnetic.

buildup.text: Ferromagnetic materials — iron, cobalt, nickel — have atomic magnetic moments that align in domains.

discovery.text: Apply a field and domains grow and align — remove it and some alignment remains as permanent magnetization.

twist.text: Above the Curie temperature, thermal energy destroys magnetic order — iron loses magnetism at 770°C.

climax.text: Neodymium magnets produce fields strong enough to levitate frogs — rare earth elements revolutionized magnets.

punchline.text: Magnetism is atoms voting together — and temperature can break the consensus.

quiz.question: What happens to a ferromagnet above its Curie temperature?
